key_insight: Flexible asymmetric leaflets in an oscillating confined channel can collectively rectify low-Re flow, and their interaction is strongest at high leaflet density and at an optimal elastoviscous balance.
engineering_relevance: The results provide design rules for passive flow rectification and transport control in microfluidic devices and biologically inspired pumping architectures.
method: Numerical study of multiple asymmetric leaflets in a confined channel at low Reynolds number
Use symmetrically oscillating plates to remove background pressure-driven asymmetry
Derive a steady-state analytical transport model and extend it to time-dependent oscillatory forcing
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model identifies a leaflet-density regime and an optimal elastoviscous number that maximize net transport.
watch_item: The framework is developed in an idealized low-Re oscillatory setting, so performance may shift when geometry, material response, or forcing conditions depart from the modeled assumptions.
paper_title: On the rectification of oscillatory flows by flexible leaflets in a confined geometry
